what_changes: Providers scheduled per shift (mean people, baseline -> policy): day 07-15: 15.0 -> 16.0; evening 15-23: 15.2 -> 16.0; night 23-07: 7.0 -> 7.0. Scheduled provider-hours per day 297 -> 312.

Nurses scheduled per shift (mean people, baseline -> policy): day 07-15: 37.0 -> 21.2 (by weekday 18.0-37.0); evening 15-23: 37.0 -> 37.0; night 23-07: 18.0 -> 21.2 (by weekday 18.0-37.0). Scheduled nurse-hours per day 736 -> 635.
Provider time between new patients and dispositions: baseline favor new 67%, favor dispositions 33% -> policy favor new 100%.
Ward early discharge rounds (share of days): baseline standard 100% -> policy standard 24%, early rounds 76%.
Overtime call-in requests: 0.00 -> 0.17 per day (one rn 0.17/day); most often at 13:00, 14:00, 15:00.
Staffing follows the published weekday arrival pattern: +0.06 provider levels and +0.08 nurse levels per 5% that the weekday runs above average.

Call-in triggers: a nurse when patients waiting for a bay exceed 80% of the ED's bay count, a provider when patients waiting for a provider exceed 49% of it; thresholds drop by up to 3% when the next hour is forecast 50% busier than typical; also a nurse when bay occupancy exceeds 95% with a typical-or-busier hour ahead.
Hallway overflow opens when patients waiting for a bay exceed 49% of the bay count (second tier at 98%).
Early ward discharge rounds are triggered when ward occupancy exceeds 77% or boarders exceed 29% of the bay count at midnight.
Provider time shifts to new patients when those waiting for a provider exceed 40% of the bay count.
People counts above use ensemble member 0's level-to-people ladder (the point calibration); the ladders differ between ensemble members, the policy's staffing LEVELS are the same in all of them.

protocol.note: Simulated. Calibrated to public aggregates; not validated on the hospital's operational data. Intervals are 95% bootstrap over twins and seeds, paired with the baseline on the same patients.
